solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Champion endlessly consuming a liqueur

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing up, so the shortened champion takes the letter inside itself
endlessly means the last letter of the word for champion is dropped

parts.note: to champion a cause is to be its advocate, a supporter who speaks up for it

explanation.surface: A cause's champion, tirelessly knocking back a sweet drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims ADVOCATE to ADVOCAT, and 'consuming' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocaat is a Dutch egg-and-brandy liqueur, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: A container partly open

parts.note: a jar is a container for jam or preserves

explanation.surface: A box or tin left with its lid half off.
explanation.definitionFit: A door that is slightly open, not shut and not wide, is said to stand that way.

clue.text: Musical composer renovated drive

indicators.note: renovated means rebuilt or done up, so the letters of drive are rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer has had the driveway of his house resurfaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian who wrote operas such as Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: Map with royal residence and public school

parts.note: a chart is a map, especially one used at sea
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen and so for royal
a house is a residence, a place to live

explanation.surface: A plan of a palace grounds next to a grand school.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'public school' is an old fee-paying private school; Charterhouse is one, in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Charterhouse is one of the historic English fee-paying boarding schools traditionally called public schools.

clue.text: Uncovered tall conifer and plant from mountainous region

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer letters, leaving only the inside of tall

parts.note: a pine is a cone-bearing evergreen tree

explanation.surface: A tall exposed conifer and other plants growing up in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine plants are those growing high in mountains, above the tree line, such as edelweiss.

clue.text: Finally exit drinking venue that gives skiers a lift

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word exit

parts.note: a bar is a place where drinks are served

explanation.surface: At the end of the day skiers leave the bar and get a ride up the slope.
explanation.definitionFit: This ski tow has a bar shaped like an inverted T that pulls two skiers uphill.

clue.text: A source of wealth, bigwig backed Antipodean soldier largely

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the word for bigwig is read in reverse

parts.note: a nob is a slang word for an important or upper-class person

indicators.note: largely means most of it, so the last letter of the soldier's word goes

parts.note: an Anzac is a soldier of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps

explanation.surface: A rich find, a big shot sponsoring an Australian soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns NOB into BON; 'largely' cuts ANZAC to ANZA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonanza was originally a rich vein of ore, hence any windfall or rich supply of money.

clue.text: Indicate movement of tigers with hesitation

indicators.note: movement suggests the letters of tigers shift about into a new order

parts.note: er is the sound a speaker makes while hesitating

explanation.surface: The big cats prowl, pausing hesitantly as they go.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauge or a face can register a reading or a feeling, that is, show or record it.

clue.text: Maybe maroon and gold cape concealed top racehorse

parts.note: to maroon someone is to abandon them, and desert is one way to do that
or is the heraldic word for gold
C is the map abbreviation for cape
concealed means hid, kept out of sight

explanation.surface: A racing colours scheme of maroon and gold, a cape hiding the champion horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert Orchid was a celebrated grey British steeplechaser that won the Cheltenham Gold Cup in 1989.

clue.text: Large blood vessel found in zebra or tapir

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the run zebra or tapir

explanation.surface: An anatomy note about a big artery in two animals at the zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the main artery, leaving the heart's left ventricle, the body's largest.

clue.text: Swine seizes two keys and two notes, money used abroad once

indicators.note: seizes means grabs and holds, so the swine word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a pig is a swine
F and E are two musical keys
N is an abbreviation for note, so two notes give two Ns

explanation.surface: A greedy man grabs keys and banknotes, cash from a foreign country long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The pfennig was the small coin of Germany, a hundredth of a mark, before the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Poet joins economist somewhere in Buckinghamshire

parts.note: John Milton was the English poet who wrote Paradise Lost
John Maynard Keynes was the influential British economist

explanation.surface: A poet and an economist team up somewhere in the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Buckinghamshire is an English county north-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton Keynes is a large planned new town in the county, so it is one place there.

clue.text: Landed gentleman bears right, then left, finding arboreal animal

indicators.note: bears means carries within, so the gentleman holds the right letter

parts.note: a squire is a country gentleman owning land

explanation.surface: A country gent, out walking, takes a right then a left and spots a creature in the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreal means tree-dwelling, and this bushy-tailed rodent lives in woods.

clue.text: Person who's pursued landing-place around banks of river

indicators.note: around means placed about, so the landing-place encloses the riverbank letters

parts.note: a quay is a wharf where boats land

indicators.note: banks are the edges, so the outer letters of river are taken

explanation.surface: A fugitive chased along a quay by the riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter's prey or the target of a chase is described by this word.

clue.text: Seamen reflecting at home drink no alcohol

parts.note: ABs are able seamen

indicators.note: reflecting means mirrored, so the word at is read backwards

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Sailors musing at home decide to go on the wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain, particularly from drinking, as a teetotaller does.

clue.text: A seductress free from worry

parts.note: a tease is a flirt who leads others on

explanation.surface: A temptress who seems utterly relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be relaxed and comfortable, without anxiety, is to be in this state.

clue.text: Visit work building firstly in very filthy place

indicators.note: in says the work and the first letter go inside the filthy place

parts.note: a sty, a pigsty, is a byword for a very dirty place
op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: firstly points to the opening letter of building

explanation.surface: Call in at a building job in a disgustingly dirty spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in on someone briefly is a phrasal verb with the same meaning as visit.

clue.text: Popular drink of spirits to arrange promptly in USA

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a short is a small measure of spirits like whisky
to order things is to arrange them

explanation.surface: Organising a round of whisky at a fashionable American bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, especially common in American English, means quickly, without delay.

clue.text: Religious books are about Greek goddess

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the books and are read backwards together

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of religious books

explanation.surface: Scriptures discuss a deity from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses, minor goddesses, presiding over love poetry.

clue.text: Hut's organised in this way

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shed tidied up in the following manner.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means so, or in the manner described.

clue.text: Republican, having paused curiously, gets info from books?

indicators.note: curiously means oddly, so the letters of paused are scrambled

explanation.surface: A US politician, having stopped for a moment, does his homework.
explanation.definitionFit: To study a subject by reading about it is an idiom for researching; the question mark admits other sources.

clue.text: Barren open country hot after high temperature

indicators.note: after means the letter for hot comes following the word for temperature

parts.note: heat is a high temperature
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Wasteland baking in the hot sun after a heatwave.
explanation.definitionFit: This is uncultivated land covered with heather and scrub, like moorland.

clue.text: Cat regularly playing — a sign of affection

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of playing is taken

parts.note: an X at the end of a letter stands for a kiss

explanation.surface: A cat at play nuzzles its owner fondly.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild member of the feline family with tufted ears.

clue.text: Audibly agreed with doctor before operations which may improve one's sight

indicators.note: audibly signals that the word for agreed is heard, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: aye is a yes, the word of someone who has agreed
ops is short for operations

explanation.surface: Having consented, a patient sees the doctor ahead of surgery to correct vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid medicine dripped into the eyes to treat infection or dryness can help vision.
